speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I need to assess the newborn presenting with respiratory distress; could you please provide the gestational age and birth weight? Additionally, has there been any maternal infection during pregnancy or signs of meconium-stained amniotic fluid?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Doctor
text: Is there any history of maternal fever, chorioamnionitis, or prolonged rupture of membranes? Have you observed any grunting, nasal flaring, or retractions during the infant's breathing efforts?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Tachypnea, Subcostal and intercostal retractions, Nasal flaring, Cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of a preterm infant with maternal diabetes, combined with ground-glass opacities on the chest X-ray and respiratory acidosis, is classic for Respiratory Distress Syndrome due to surfactant deficiency. DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS)
